title: Data structures
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Implement and analyze the core data structures: abstract data types, dynamic arrays and amortized analysis, linked lists, stacks, queues and deques, hash tables, trees and binary search trees, balanced search trees, heaps and priority queues, graphs, tries and union–find.

weeks.1: Abstract data types and big-O review
weeks.6: Hash table design: load factor and resizing
weeks.9: Balanced search trees: AVL and red-black ideas
weeks.12: Choosing data structures: tries and union–find

blocks.deliverable: Implement a dynamic array and measure its growth.
Implement a linked list and a queue with tests.
Implement a hash map with chaining.
Week 7 midterm; implement a binary search tree with insert, search and in-order traversal.
Implement breadth-first and depth-first search on an adjacency list.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Build a small library of data structures (dynamic array, linked list, hash map, binary search tree, heap and graph) with full tests and a report comparing measured running times with big-O predictions; then use the library to build a word index or a route finder.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
